sanskrit: viduraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca mahārājaṃ ca bāhlikam kṛpaṃ ca somadattaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ janārdanam
english: Vidura and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great king Bahlika, Kṛpa and Somadatta, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Janārdana —

sanskrit: sarvān etān anādṛtya durmatir nirapatrapaḥ aśiṣṭavad amaryādo mānī mānyāvamānitā
english: Disregarding all of them, that evil-minded, shameless man, behaving rudely and without propriety, arrogant, yet scorning those who deserve honour,

sanskrit: taṃ prasthitam abhiprekṣya bhrātaro manujarṣabham anujagmuḥ sahāmātyā rājānaś cāpi sarvaśaḥ
english: Seeing that bull among men depart, his brothers followed him together with counsellors, and kings followed on every side.

sanskrit: sabhāyām utthitaṃ kruddhaṃ prasthitaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha duryodhanam abhiprekṣya bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt
english: Seeing Duryodhana rise in anger from the assembly and depart together with his brothers, Bhīṣma, son of Shantanu, spoke:

sanskrit: dharmārthāv abhisaṃtyajya saṃrambhaṃ yo 'numanyate hasanti vyasane tasya durhṛdo nacirād iva
english: Those who sanction wrath while abandoning dharma and artha — their enemies rejoice at their misfortune before long.

sanskrit: durātmā rājaputro 'yaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nupāyavit mithyābhimānī rājyasya krodhalobhavaśānugaḥ
english: This wicked-souled prince, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, knows no proper policy; he is falsely proud of his kingdom, and is enslaved by anger and greed.

sanskrit: kālapakvam idaṃ manye sarvakṣatraṃ janārdana sarve hy anusṛtā mohāt pārthivāḥ saha mantribhiḥ
english: I think the entire warrior order is ripe for its time, O Janārdana, for all the kings along with their ministers have followed him out of delusion.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasyātha vacaḥ śrutvā dāśārhaḥ puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ bhīṣmadroṇamukhān sarvān abhyabhāṣata vīryavān
english: Hearing Bhīṣma's words, the mighty Dāśārha of lotus eyes addressed all those headed by Bhīṣma and Droṇa:

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ kuruvṛddhānāṃ mahān ayam atikramaḥ prasahya mandam aiśvarye na niyacchata yan nṛpam
english: This is a great transgression against all the elders of the Kurus — that you do not forcibly restrain this foolish king from wielding power.

sanskrit: tatra kāryam ahaṃ manye prāptakālam ariṃdamāḥ kriyamāṇe bhavec chreyas tat sarvaṃ śṛṇutānaghāḥ
english: I deem that the timely action to be taken there is this — listen all of you, O destroyers of foes, O sinless ones: if it is done, good will come of it.

sanskrit: pratyakṣam etad bhavatāṃ yad vakṣyāmi hitaṃ vacaḥ bhavatām ānukūlyena yadi roceta bhāratāḥ
english: What I shall speak is beneficial counsel that is evident to all of you — if it pleases you, O Bharatas, with your agreement.

sanskrit: bhojarājasya vṛddhasya durācāro hy anātmavān jīvataḥ pitur aiśvaryaṃ hṛtvā manyuvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Kaṃsa, the ill-conducted and self-abandoned son of the old Bhoja king, seized his living father's power and fell under the sway of wrath.

sanskrit: ugrasenasutaḥ kaṃsaḥ parityaktaḥ sa bāndhavaiḥ jñātīnāṃ hitakāmena mayā śasto mahāmṛdhe
english: Kaṃsa, son of Ugrasena, was abandoned by his kinsmen, and was slain by me in great battle for the welfare of our clan.

sanskrit: āhukaḥ punar asmābhir jñātibhiś cāpi satkṛtaḥ ugrasenaḥ kṛto rājā bhojarājanyavardhanaḥ
english: Then Ahuka — Ugrasena — was honoured by us and by our kinsmen and was made king, the enhancer of the Bhoja royal line.

sanskrit: kaṃsam ekaṃ parityajya kulārthe sarvayādavāḥ saṃbhūya sukham edhante bhāratāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ
english: Abandoning Kaṃsa alone for the sake of the family, all the Yādavas together — the Bharata Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis — thrive in happiness.

sanskrit: api cāpy avadad rājan parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ vyūḍhe devāsure yuddhe 'bhyudyateṣv āyudheṣu ca
english: Moreover, O king, Parameṣṭhin the lord of creatures spoke, when the divine-demonic war was arrayed and weapons were raised:

sanskrit: dvaidhībhūteṣu lokeṣu vinaśyatsu ca bhārata abravīt sṛṣṭimān devo bhagavāṃl lokabhāvanaḥ
english: When the worlds were split into two factions and were perishing, O Bharata, the lord god, the creator and sustainer of worlds, spoke:

sanskrit: parābhaviṣyanty asurā daiteyā dānavaiḥ saha ādityā vasavo rudrā bhaviṣyanti divaukasaḥ
english: The Asuras — Daityas together with Dānavas — shall be defeated; the Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudras shall prevail as the heaven-dwellers.

sanskrit: devāsuramanuṣyāś ca gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ asmin yuddhe susaṃyattā haniṣyanti parasparam
english: Gods, demons, humans, Gandharvas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, fully arrayed in this battle, shall slay one another.

sanskrit: iti matvābravīd dharmaṃ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ varuṇāya prayacchaitān baddhvā daiteyadānavān
english: Having thought thus, Parameṣṭhin the lord of creatures spoke to Dharma: 'Bind the Daityas and Dānavas and hand them over to Varuṇa.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tato dharmo niyogāt parameṣṭhinaḥ varuṇāya dadau sarvān baddhvā daiteyadānavān
english: So spoken to, Dharma, by Parameṣṭhin's command, bound all the Daityas and Dānavas and delivered them to Varuṇa.

sanskrit: tān baddhvā dharmapāśaiś ca svaiś ca pāśair jaleśvaraḥ varuṇaḥ sāgare yatto nityaṃ rakṣati dānavān
english: Having bound them with bonds of Dharma and with his own bonds, Varuṇa the lord of waters guards the Dānavas in the ocean, ever vigilant.

sanskrit: tathā duryodhanaṃ karṇaṃ śakuniṃ cāpi saubalam baddhvā duḥśāsanaṃ cāpi pāṇḍavebhyaḥ prayacchata
english: Likewise, bind Duryodhana, Karṇa, Śakuni the son of Subala, and Duḥśāsana as well, and hand them over to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tyajet kulārthe puruṣaṃ grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet
english: One should abandon a person for the sake of the family; abandon a family for the sake of a village; abandon a village for the sake of the kingdom; and abandon the earth for the sake of the self.

sanskrit: rājan duryodhanaṃ baddhvā tataḥ saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ tvatkṛte na vinaśyeyuḥ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: O king, bind Duryodhana and then make peace with the Pāṇḍavas; for your sake, O bull among warriors, let not the warriors be destroyed.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛṣṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ viduraṃ sarvadharmajñaṃ tvaramāṇo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Kṛṣṇa's words, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, hastily addressed Vidura, who knows all dharma:

sanskrit: gaccha tāta mahāprājñāṃ gāndhārīṃ dīrghadarśinīm ānayeha tayā sārdham anuneṣyāmi durmatim
english: Go, dear one, and bring here the greatly wise Gāndhārī, she of far sight; together with her I will appease this evil-minded son.

sanskrit: yadi sāpi durātmānaṃ śamayed duṣṭacetasam api kṛṣṇāya suhṛdas tiṣṭhema vacane vayam
english: If she too should calm this wicked-minded, corrupt-hearted one, then we too can stand as friends in accord with Kṛṣṇa's counsel.

sanskrit: api lobhābhibhūtasya panthānam anudarśayet durbuddher duḥsahāyasya samarthaṃ bruvatī vacaḥ
english: Speaking capable words, she might show the right path to this one overcome by greed, of wicked intellect and evil companions.

sanskrit: api no vyasanaṃ ghoraṃ duryodhanakṛtaṃ mahat śamayec cirarātrāya yogakṣemavad avyayam
english: She might also quell this great and dreadful calamity brought about by Duryodhana, so that lasting security and welfare may endure for us.

sanskrit: rājñas tu vacanaṃ śrutvā viduro dīrghadarśinīm ānayām āsa gāndhārīṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śāsanāt
english: Hearing the king's words, Vidura, by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's order, brought Gāndhārī of far sight.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca eṣa gāndhāri putras te durātmā śāsanātigaḥ aiśvaryalobhād aiśvaryaṃ jīvitaṃ ca prahāsyati
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: This son of yours, Gāndhārī, is wicked-souled and transgresses all command; out of greed for power he will forfeit both power and life.

sanskrit: aśiṣṭavad amaryādaḥ pāpaiḥ saha durātmabhiḥ sabhāyā nirgato mūḍho vyatikramya suhṛdvacaḥ
english: Behaving rudely and without propriety, in the company of sinful and wicked men, this fool has left the assembly, transgressing the counsel of his well-wishers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā bhartur vacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrī yaśasvinī anvicchantī mahac chreyo gāndhārī vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That glorious princess, hearing her husband's words and seeking the greater good, Gāndhārī spoke:

sanskrit: ānayeha sutaṃ kṣipraṃ rājyakāmukam āturam na hi rājyam aśiṣṭena śakyaṃ dharmārthalopinā
english: Bring here quickly this son who is so agitated in his craving for the kingdom — for one who is rude and who abandons dharma and artha cannot hold a kingdom.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hy evātra bhṛśaṃ garhyo dhṛtarāṣṭra sutapriyaḥ yo jānan pāpatām asya tatprajñām anuvartase
english: You yourself are greatly blameworthy here, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, so fond of your son — for knowing his wickedness, you follow the bent of his intellect.

sanskrit: sa eṣa kāmamanyubhyāṃ pralabdho moham āsthitaḥ aśakyo 'dya tvayā rājan vinivartayituṃ balāt
english: This man, deluded and overcome by desire and anger, has now settled into confusion; he cannot today be turned back by you by force, O king.

sanskrit: rājyapradāne mūḍhasya bāliśasya durātmanaḥ duḥsahāyasya lubdhasya dhṛtarāṣṭro 'śnute phalam
english: By giving the kingdom to this foolish, childish, wicked-souled, evil-companioned, and greedy man, Dhṛtarāṣṭra reaps the fruit.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi svajane bhedam upekṣeta mahāmatiḥ bhinnaṃ hi svajanena tvāṃ prasahiṣyanti śatravaḥ
english: How can a great-minded man overlook division among his own people? When your own people are divided against you, your enemies will overpower you.

sanskrit: yā hi śakyā mahārāja sāmnā dānena vā punaḥ nistartum āpadaḥ sveṣu daṇḍaṃ kas tatra pātayet
english: Those calamities that can be overcome among one's own people by conciliation or by gifts — who would apply punishment there, O great king?

sanskrit: śāsanād dhṛtarāṣṭrasya duryodhanam amarṣaṇam mātuś ca vacanāt kṣattā sabhāṃ prāveśayat punaḥ
english: By order of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the word of his mother, Kṣattā (Vidura) brought the impatient Duryodhana back into the assembly.

sanskrit: sa mātur vacanākāṅkṣī praviveśa sabhāṃ punaḥ abhitāmrekṣaṇaḥ krodhān niḥśvasann iva pannagaḥ
english: Desirous of hearing his mother's words, he entered the assembly again — his eyes flushed red all around, hissing in anger like a serpent.

sanskrit: taṃ praviṣṭam abhiprekṣya putram utpatham āsthitam vigarhamāṇā gāndhārī samarthaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing her son who had entered, who had taken to a wrong path, Gāndhārī reproached him and spoke these fitting words:

sanskrit: duryodhana nibodhedaṃ vacanaṃ mama putraka hitaṃ te sānubandhasya tathāyatyāṃ sukhodayam
english: Duryodhana, hear this word of mine, dear son — it is for your good and for those bound to you, and will bring happiness in the future.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya tu pituś caiva mama cāpacitiḥ kṛtā bhaved droṇamukhānāṃ ca suhṛdāṃ śāmyatā tvayā
english: By your becoming calm, reverence would be shown to Bhīṣma, to your father, to me, and to the well-wishers headed by Droṇa.

sanskrit: na hi rājyaṃ mahāprājña svena kāmena śakyate avāptuṃ rakṣituṃ vāpi bhoktuṃ vā bharatarṣabha
english: O greatly wise one, O bull of the Bharatas, a kingdom cannot be won, protected, or enjoyed by one's own mere desire.

sanskrit: na hy avaśyendriyo rājyam aśnīyād dīrgham antaram vijitātmā tu medhāvī sa rājyam abhipālayet
english: One whose senses are ungoverned cannot enjoy a kingdom for a long time; but the intelligent man who has conquered himself can protect a kingdom.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau hi puruṣam arthebhyo vyapakarṣataḥ tau tu śatrū vinirjitya rājā vijayate mahīm
english: Desire and anger drag a man away from his purposes; but a king who conquers those two enemies gains the earth.

sanskrit: lokeśvaraprabhutvaṃ hi mahad etad durātmabhiḥ rājyaṃ nāmepsitaṃ sthānaṃ na śakyam abhirakṣitum
english: This great lordship over the world — a kingdom, that coveted station — cannot be protected by those of wicked soul.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi mahat prepsur niyacched arthadharmayoḥ indriyair niyatair buddhir vardhate 'gnir ivendhanaiḥ
english: One who seeks greatness must restrain the senses in accordance with artha and dharma; with restrained senses, intellect grows as fire grows with fuel.

sanskrit: avidhyeyāni hīmāni vyāpādayitum apy alam avidheyā ivādāntā hayāḥ pathi kusārathim
english: These uncontrollable senses are indeed capable of ruining one — like unruly, untamed horses on the road ruin a poor charioteer.

sanskrit: avijitya ya ātmānam amātyān vijigīṣate ajitātmājitāmātyaḥ so 'vaśaḥ parihīyate
english: He who seeks to conquer ministers without having conquered himself — with self unconquered and ministers unconquered — falls away without mastery.

sanskrit: ātmānam eva prathamaṃ deśarūpeṇa yo jayet tato 'mātyān amitrāṃś ca na moghaṃ vijigīṣate
english: He who first conquers himself in the manner appropriate to the situation — then conquers ministers and enemies — does not strive in vain.

sanskrit: vaśyendriyaṃ jitāmātyaṃ dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ vikāriṣu parīkṣyakāriṇaṃ dhīram atyantaṃ śrīr niṣevate
english: Prosperity constantly attends one whose senses are subdued, whose ministers are won over, who wields authority over transgressors, who acts with deliberation, and who is steady.

sanskrit: kṣudrākṣeṇeva jālena jhaṣāv apihitāv ubhau kāmakrodhau śarīrasthau prajñānaṃ tau vilumpataḥ
english: Like two fish covered by a fine-meshed net, desire and anger, dwelling in the body, plunder one's wisdom.

sanskrit: yābhyāṃ hi devāḥ svaryātuḥ svargasyāpidadhur mukham bibhyato 'nuparāgasya kāmakrodhau sma vardhitau
english: It was desire and anger, when nurtured and fearing eclipse, that caused the gods to travel to heaven and close the door of heaven.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca dambhaṃ darpaṃ ca bhūmipaḥ samyag vijetuṃ yo veda sa mahīm abhijāyate
english: The king who knows how to fully conquer desire, anger, greed, arrogance, and pride — he is truly born to rule the earth.

sanskrit: satataṃ nigrahe yukta indriyāṇāṃ bhaven nṛpaḥ īpsann arthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca dviṣatāṃ ca parābhavam
english: A king who seeks artha, dharma, and the downfall of his enemies must be constantly engaged in restraining the senses.

sanskrit: kāmābhibhūtaḥ krodhād vā yo mithyā pratipadyate sveṣu cānyeṣu vā tasya na sahāyā bhavanty uta
english: He who, overcome by desire or anger, proceeds wrongly toward his own people or toward others — for him there are no allies.

sanskrit: ekībhūtair mahāprājñaiḥ śūrair arinibarhaṇaiḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ pṛthivīṃ tāta bhokṣyase sahitaḥ sukhī
english: United with the greatly wise, heroic, foe-crushing Pāṇḍavas, dear son, you will enjoy the earth happily together.

sanskrit: yathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo droṇaś cāpi mahārathaḥ āhatus tāta tat satyam ajeyau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: As Bhīṣma son of Shantanu and the great warrior Droṇa have said, dear son — that is the truth: Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍavas are unconquerable.

sanskrit: prapadyasva mahābāhuṃ kṛṣṇam akliṣṭakāriṇam prasanno hi sukhāya syād ubhayor eva keśavaḥ
english: Surrender to mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, the tireless doer of deeds; for Keśava, when pleased, would be for the happiness of both sides.

sanskrit: suhṛdām arthakāmānāṃ yo na tiṣṭhati śāsane prājñānāṃ kṛtavidyānāṃ sa naraḥ śatrunandanaḥ
english: The man who does not abide by the counsel of well-wishers who desire his good, of the wise and learned — that man is a delight to his enemies.

sanskrit: na yuddhe tāta kalyāṇaṃ na dharmārthau kutaḥ sukham na cāpi vijayo nityaṃ mā yuddhe ceta ādhithāḥ
english: There is no good in war, dear son; neither dharma nor artha — whence happiness? Nor is victory assured; set not your mind on war.

sanskrit: bhīṣmeṇa hi mahāprājña pitrā te bāhlikena ca datto 'ṃśaḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ bhedād bhītair ariṃdama
english: O greatly wise one, O crusher of enemies, Bhīṣma and your father and Bahlika, fearing division, gave a share to the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tasya caitat pradānasya phalam adyānupaśyasi yadbhuṅkṣe pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ śūrair nihatakaṇṭakām
english: You see today the fruit of that gift — you enjoy the whole earth with its thorns removed by those heroes.

sanskrit: prayaccha pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ yathocitam ariṃdama yadīcchasi sahāmātyo bhoktum ardhaṃ mahīkṣitām
english: Give to the sons of Pāṇḍu what is proper, O crusher of enemies, if you wish to enjoy, together with your ministers, half of the kingdom of earth.

sanskrit: alam ardhaṃ pṛthivyās te sahāmātyasya jīvanam suhṛdāṃ vacane tiṣṭhan yaśaḥ prāpsyasi bhārata
english: Half the earth is enough for your life together with your ministers; standing by the counsel of well-wishers, you shall attain fame, O Bharata.

sanskrit: śrīmadbhir ātmavadbhir hi buddhimadbhir jitendriyaiḥ pāṇḍavair vigrahas tāta bhraṃśayen mahataḥ sukhāt
english: Conflict with the prosperous, self-possessed, wise, and sense-subduing Pāṇḍavas, dear son, would cause you to fall from great happiness.

sanskrit: nigṛhya suhṛdāṃ manyuṃ śādhi rājyaṃ yathocitam svam aṃśaṃ pāṇḍuputrebhyaḥ pradāya bharatarṣabha
english: Restraining the resentment of well-wishers, rule the kingdom as is proper, having given the Pāṇḍavas their share, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: alam ahnā nikāro 'yaṃ trayodaśa samāḥ kṛtaḥ śamayainaṃ mahāprājña kāmakrodhasamedhitam
english: Enough — this insult has been sustained for thirteen years; pacify it now, O greatly wise one — this anger and resentment that has been inflamed by desire and wrath.

sanskrit: na caiṣa śaktaḥ pārthānāṃ yas tvadartham abhīpsati sūtaputro dṛḍhakrodho bhrātā duḥśāsanaś ca te
english: Neither the charioteer's son of firm anger who desires your cause, nor your brother Duḥśāsana, is capable against the Pārthas.

sanskrit: bhīṣme droṇe kṛpe karṇe bhīmasene dhanaṃjaye dhṛṣṭadyumne ca saṃkruddhe na syuḥ sarvāḥ prajā dhruvam
english: When Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, Bhīmasena, Dhanañjaya, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna are all enraged, all the people assuredly cannot stand.

sanskrit: amarṣavaśam āpanno mā kurūṃs tāta jīghanaḥ sarvā hi pṛthivī spṛṣṭā tvat pāṇḍavakṛte vadham
english: Overcome by impatience, do not seek to destroy the Kurus, dear son; for the whole earth is drawn into destruction on account of you and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yac ca tvaṃ manyase mūḍha bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādayaḥ yotsyante sarvaśaktyeti naitad adyopapadyate
english: And as for what you think, O fool — that Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa and the rest will fight with all their might — that does not hold today.

sanskrit: samaṃ hi rājyaṃ prītiś ca sthānaṃ ca vijitātmanām pāṇḍaveṣv atha yuṣmāsu dharmas tv abhyadhikas tataḥ
english: For those who have conquered themselves, the kingdom, affection, and position are equal among the Pāṇḍavas and among you; but dharma is greater on their side.

sanskrit: rājapiṇḍabhayād ete yadi hāsyanti jīvitam na hi śakṣyanti rājānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram udīkṣitum
english: If these men give up their lives out of fear of their royal obligation, they still shall not be able to face King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: na lobhād arthasaṃpattir narāṇām iha dṛśyate tad alaṃ tāta lobhena praśāmya bharatarṣabha
english: Prosperity of men through greed is not seen here; therefore enough of greed, dear son — be calm, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tat tu vākyam anādṛtya so 'rthavan mātṛbhāṣitam punaḥ pratasthe saṃrambhāt sakāśam akṛtātmanām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But disregarding that meaningful word spoken by his mother, he departed again in anger toward those of unconquered selves.

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhāyā nirgamya mantrayām āsa kauravaḥ saubalena matākṣeṇa rājñā śakuninā saha
english: Then, having left the assembly, that Kaurava held counsel with Śakuni, son of Subala, the dice-shrewd king.
